The program allows students to develop highly focused expertise in a particular policy area, while also becoming versatile in the multiple methodologies of public policy analysis. Our students work closely with the Goldman School faculty and are encouraged to collaborate with other faculty and doctoral students across the UC Berkeley campus.
column51: $34,000 stipend plus full tuition and fees
column101: Merit-based (multi-year funding package including fellowships, GSI, and GSR positions)

column2: Master of Science in Range Management
column16: Minimum requirements for admission: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; A satisfactory scholastic record, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Additional Program Requirements: Letters of Recommendation (3), Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Resume/CV. The GRE General Test is not required.
column47: The Range Management Graduate Group offers a program of study leading to an MS degree in Range Management. This program is coordinated by the Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management. Range management is the specialized system of land management used to provide consumer goods and ecosystem services from non-arable lands. These lands, which include grasslands, shrublands, woodlands, and deserts, are managed by ecological rather than agronomic methods. The master’s program is designed to provide students with a) a solid foundation in the concepts and methods of range management and b) an opportunity to explore a specific problem in range management. It is particularly suited to students who have a bachelor’s degree in range management, forestry, or a related field and who wish to pursue a career in the management of rangeland resources.

column2: Master of Real Estate Development + Design
column16: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0. Application requirements include an online application, official transcripts, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, and a current resume. International applicants from countries where the official language is not English must submit evidence of English language proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS).
column47: The Master of Real Estate Development + Design (MRED+D) at UC Berkeley’s College of Environmental Design is an intensive, 11-month professional graduate degree program. Our curriculum centers on the four pillars of real estate development: finance, design, law, and construction. It also uniquely incorporates the principles of equity, sustainability, and resilience, preparing you to lead the creation of sustainable and vibrant urban environments. The program is designed to bridge the gap between design and real estate development, equipping students with the skills to address the complex challenges of urban development in the 21st century.

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Rhetoric
column16: Application requirements for the Doctor of Philosophy in Rhetoric include: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, Personal history statement, Writing sample (approximately 20–30 pages), and a Resume/CV. The Rhetoric department is a leading center for the study of the history and theory of rhetoric in its diverse forms: through legal and political arguments, in the literary and the visual arts, and as a philosophical and ethical practice.
column47: The Rhetoric Department is a leading center for interdisciplinary research in the humanities and social sciences. The program's strength is its multifaceted approach to the study of the history and theory of rhetorical discourse in its various forms: political, legal, scientific, and aesthetic. Rhetoric is also a primary site for the study of contemporary theory and for the development of new approaches to the study of images and visual culture. The department's faculty is known for its wide-ranging intellectual reach, and its graduate students often pursue research that crosses traditional disciplinary boundaries.
column101: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researchers (GSR)

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Romance Languages and Literatures
column16: The Romance Languages and Literatures (RLL) program at UC Berkeley is a joint program that allows students to specialize in two or more Romance languages (French, Italian, and Spanish) and their literatures. Minimum requirements for admission include a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution, and a grade point average of at least 3.0 (B). The RLL program requires its students to be proficient in at least two Romance languages. At least one of these should be at the level of a native speaker or a student with an undergraduate major in that language/literature. To be admitted, you should have at least some knowledge of the second language. Knowledge of a third Romance language is desirable, though not required for admission.
column47: The interdisciplinary PhD program in Romance Languages and Literatures (RLL) is offered by the departments of French, Italian Studies, and Spanish & Portuguese. Candidates work toward the PhD in Romance Languages and Literatures with an emphasis on a combination of two of the three Romance languages/literatures: French, Italian, and Spanish/Portuguese. The RLL program is designed for students whose interest in these languages and literatures and their corresponding cultures and linguistics requires a broader angle of vision than is found in a single-language department. Students specialize in two of the languages/literatures taught in the three departments (French, Italian, Spanish & Portuguese). One is designated as the student's major language, the other as the minor language. Students take courses in both languages and literatures, and they may be asked to teach in both. RLL students are also encouraged to make use of Berkeley’s many other departments and programs (e.g., Comparative Literature, Film Studies, Linguistics, Women’s Studies) to further their research and help form their dissertation committees.
column101: Merit-based

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Scandinavian Languages and Literatures
column16: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0. Required application materials include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, a writing sample (typically 15-20 pages), and a current CV/resume.
column47: The Department of Scandinavian offers a program of study leading to the MA and PhD in Scandinavian languages and literatures. The program is designed to provide students with a broad knowledge of Scandinavian literature, culture, and linguistics, and a high level of proficiency in at least one Scandinavian language. Students specialize in either the medieval or the modern period.
column101: Merit-based fellowships

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Slavic Languages and Literatures
column16: Prospective applicants must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. At least two years of Russian or another Slavic language are required for admission to the program. Applicants must have a grade point average of at least 3.0 (B) or the equivalent in all work completed after the first two years of undergraduate study. The department requires three letters of recommendation and a writing sample of 15–20 pages. Applicants must also provide a Statement of Purpose and a Personal History Statement.
column46: Russian Literature, Czech Literature, Polish Literature, South Slavic Literature, or Slavic Linguistics
column47: The Department of Slavic Languages and Literatures offers programs of study leading to the MA and PhD degrees. Students are required to choose a major field (Russian, Czech, Polish, or South Slavic literatures or Slavic linguistics). To ensure that students receive a broad background, they must also choose two minor fields, one of which must be in a Slavic field (unless the major is Slavic linguistics, in which case both minors may be outside the field). This requirement may be satisfied by a minor in another Slavic literature or in Slavic linguistics, or by a minor in a related field such as another literature, history, or linguistics. All PhD students are required to take a pedagogy course in their second year and must complete at least two semesters of apprentice teaching. UC Berkeley Slavic graduates are distinguished by their preparation as both scholars and teachers. Members of the faculty represent a wide range of interests and approaches to the study of literature and linguistics.
column101: Fellowships, teaching assistantships, and research assistantships

column2: Master of Social Welfare
column16: To be considered for admission to the MSW program, you must meet the following minimum requirements: A bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A grade point average (GPA) of B (3.0) or better. Evidence of sufficient preparation in the liberal arts and sciences. Social Work Experience: We strongly recommend that all applicants have the equivalent of at least one year (2,100 hours) of paid or volunteer social work experience.
column47: The School of Social Welfare and the School of Public Health offer a concurrent degree program for students who wish to pursue a career in the field of public health social work. This program is designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge and skills for effective practice at the intersection of these two fields. It offers a comprehensive and integrated approach to social welfare and public health, with a focus on addressing the social determinants of health and promoting health equity. The concurrent degree program is a three-year program. It is designed to be completed in six semesters of full-time study. At the end of three years, the student will have earned both the Master of Social Welfare (MSW) and the Master of Public Health (MPH) degrees.
column50: The MSW program at UC Berkeley is fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). The UC Berkeley School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
column101: Merit-based, Need-based

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Social Welfare
column16: Applicants to the PhD program in Social Welfare must meet the following minimum requirements: a bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; a grade point average (GPA) of B (3.0) or better; evidence of capacity for doctoral-level scholarship and potential for making a significant contribution to the field of social welfare; and for most applicants, completion of a master's degree in social work or a related field. Required application materials include: Three letters of recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, Writing Sample, and a Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume.
column47: Berkeley Social Welfare’s PhD program prepares students for careers as scholars, researchers, and educators in the field of social welfare. Our program offers a rigorous, interdisciplinary curriculum designed to foster deep knowledge of social problems and the policies and practices designed to address them. Our PhD students learn to conduct independent research that contributes to the scientific knowledge base of the profession and informs social welfare policy and practice.
column101: Multi-year fellowship support (stipend plus in-state tuition and fees), Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) or Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Sociology
column16: The basic minimum requirement for admission to graduate study at Berkeley is a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution with a 3.0 grade-point average (GPA). Applicants are evaluated on the basis of their performance in previous academic work, the statement of purpose and personal history, the quality of the writing sample, and the strength of the letters of recommendation.
column47: The graduate program in sociology at Berkeley is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a Ph.D. It is primarily intended to prepare students for research and teaching in sociology, although some of our graduates also work in other fields. The department is a community of scholars including 30 faculty members and approximately 100 graduate students.
column101: Multi-year funding package (Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, and Research Assistantships)

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in South and Southeast Asian Studies
column16: The minimum graduate admission requirements are: (1) A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution; (2) A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale; and (3) Enough undergraduate training to do graduate work in your chosen field. Applicants must also submit a Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, and a Writing Sample.
column46: South Asian Studies, Southeast Asian Studies
column47: The Department of South & Southeast Asian Studies offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Arts (MA) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in South and Southeast Asian Studies. The MA and PhD programs are intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and teaching at the university level or to apply their knowledge of South or Southeast Asian languages and cultures in other professional contexts. Within the PhD program, there are two distinct tracks: South Asian Studies and Southeast Asian Studies. The South Asian Studies track is designed to provide students with a deep and wide-ranging knowledge of the languages and cultures of the South Asian subcontinent. Students choose a primary language of concentration (Sanskrit, Hindi, Urdu, Tamil, etc.) and a field of specialization (Literature, Religion, Philosophy, History, or Social Sciences). The Southeast Asian Studies track is designed to provide students with a deep and wide-ranging knowledge of the languages and cultures of the Southeast Asian region. Students choose a primary language of concentration (Indonesian, Khmer, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese, etc.) and a field of specialization (Literature, Religion, Philosophy, History, or Social Sciences).
column101: Merit-based fellowships (e.g., Berkeley Fellowship, Chancellor's Fellowship), FLAS fellowships, and teaching/research assistantships

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Spanish and Portuguese
column16: The Department of Spanish & Portuguese offers programs of study for the PhD in Spanish & Portuguese and the PhD in Hispanic Languages & Literatures. The department does not offer a terminal MA degree. Students are admitted to the PhD program. Students who have not yet earned an MA will earn the degree while working toward the PhD.
column46: Iberian and Latin American Literatures and Cultures; Luso-Brazilian Literatures and Cultures; Romance Languages and Literatures; Hispanic Languages and Literatures
column47: The graduate program in Spanish and Portuguese at Berkeley provides students with the most comprehensive education in the literatures, cultures, and languages of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds. The department offers the MA/PhD and PhD degrees in Spanish and Portuguese, with concentrations in Iberian and Latin American Literatures and Cultures and Luso-Brazilian Literatures and Cultures. We also participate in two interdisciplinary doctoral programs: Romance Languages and Literatures (offered in conjunction with the Departments of French and Italian) and Hispanic Languages and Literatures (offered in conjunction with the Department of Linguistics).
column101: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Readers

column2: Master of Arts in Statistics
column16: A bachelor's degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. For admission to the Master of Arts program, a bachelor's degree in any field is acceptable, but the applicant must have had some basic training in mathematics, including at least three semesters of calculus, a semester of linear algebra, and a semester of real analysis. In addition, some exposure to probability and statistics is desirable. International applicants from countries where the official language is not English must provide evidence of English language proficiency.
column38: Department of Statistics, College of Computing, Data Science, and Society
column47: The Department of Statistics offers three degree programs: the Ph.D., the M.A., and the Professional Master of Financial Engineering (MFE). Students in the Ph.D. program and M.A. program receive a solid foundation in statistical theory and practice. Faculty members are involved in a wide range of research projects in theoretical and applied statistics. Graduate students and faculty members benefit from the department's close ties with many researchers across the Berkeley campus and at the nearby Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. These groups offer a regular flow of visitors, many of whom give talks in the several departmental seminars. M.A. Degree: The M.A. in Statistics provides a solid foundation in statistical theory and practice and can be used as a springboard for a statistics or data science career in a variety of industries. This is a small, selective, and very fast-paced program that is usually completed in two semesters (one academic year).

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Statistics
column16: Prospective students should have a strong background in mathematics: at least three semesters of calculus, a course in linear algebra, and a course in real analysis. Some experience with probability and statistics is also desirable. Application Requirements: Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, 3 letters of recommendation, CV/Resume, Official Transcripts.
column47: The doctoral program in statistics is designed to give students a comprehensive knowledge of the theory and methods of statistics and probability. It is intended for students with a strong mathematical background and an interest in any area of statistics or probability. Research interests of faculty and students include many areas of statistical theory and methodology, probability theory, and the application of statistics and probability to many fields, including the biological and physical sciences, social sciences, and engineering.
column101: Fellowships, Graduate Student Instructorships (GSI), and Graduate Student Researcherships (GSR)

column2: Master of Translational Medicine
column16: To apply for the Master of Translational Medicine, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) on a 4.0 scale. Required application materials include three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, a Personal History Statement, and a current resume or CV. International applicants must also demonstrate English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS). Additionally, the program requires prerequisite knowledge in Calculus (one year), Physics (one year), Chemistry (one year), and Biology (one year).
column38: Department of Bioengineering (UC Berkeley) and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences (UCSF)
column47: The Master of Translational Medicine (MTM) program is a joint effort between the Department of Bioengineering at UC Berkeley and the Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences at UCSF. The program is designed to provide students with the tools and network to take a medical innovation from the lab to the clinic. The curriculum combines engineering, clinical, and business training to prepare students for careers in the biotech and medical device industries, teaching essential skills to move innovations through the pipeline from the lab to the bedside.
column101: Merit-based (MTM Departmental Scholarships)

column2: Master of Urban Design
column16: General application requirements include: official transcripts, evidence of English language proficiency (for international applicants), Statement of Purpose, Personal History Statement, three letters of recommendation, current resume/CV, and a portfolio. The GRE (Graduate Record Examination) is not required for this program.
column47: The Master of Urban Design (MUD) is a one-year (three semester) post-professional degree for those who already have a professional degree in architecture, landscape architecture, or city and regional planning. The program aims to train future leaders of urban design who can address the complex challenges of making and managing the urban environment in a rapidly urbanizing world. Urban design is an interdisciplinary field, and the program at Berkeley brings together faculty and students from the departments of Architecture, City & Regional Planning, and Landscape Architecture & Environmental Planning. The MUD program is centered on the urban design studio. Projects are based on real-world sites in the San Francisco Bay Area and elsewhere, and explore a wide range of urban scales, from the street and the block to the neighborhood and the region.
column101: Departmental fellowships, Merit-based, Need-based

column2: Doctor of Philosophy in Vision Science
column16: To apply for the Doctor of Philosophy in Vision Science, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited institution and a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of B (3.0) or better. Required application materials include transcripts for all college-level work, three letters of recommendation, a Personal History Statement, a Statement of Purpose, and a current Resume or CV. International applicants from countries where the official language is not English must provide evidence of English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS scores). The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required.
column38: Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry & Vision Science
column47: The Vision Science Graduate Program provides comprehensive training in the many aspects of vision science, from the molecular biology of the eye to the psychology and neurophysiology of perception. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. The Vision Science Program at UC Berkeley is an interdisciplinary program where students study the biology, physics, and psychology of sight and its impact on individuals and society. The program offers students a broad foundation in vision science while allowing them to specialize in a specific area of research, with access to state-of-the-art research facilities and world-renowned faculty.
column99: Full tuition and fees plus annual stipend
column101: Merit-based fellowships, Graduate Student Research (GSR) appointments, and Graduate Student Instructor (GSI) positions

column2: Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory
column16: To apply for the Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory, students must already be enrolled in a Ph.D. program at UC Berkeley. Applications are accepted twice annually. Required materials include: 1. A letter of intent (2-3 pages) describing the student’s interest in the DE, how their research relates to critical theory, and the courses they plan to take; 2. A curriculum vitae; 3. A writing sample (20-30 pages); 4. A letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor supporting the application to the DE.
column47: The Designated Emphasis in Critical Theory (DE) provides graduate students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley with a curricular and research framework for studying the history and current developments of critical theory. The program is intended to offer students a systematic approach to the diverse traditions of critical thought that have informed modern scholarship across the humanities and social sciences. Students who complete the requirements of the DE receive a certificate of completion and the designation 'Critical Theory' on their official transcript and diploma.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Folklore
column16: Admission to the designated emphasis is contingent on prior admission to a PhD program at UC Berkeley. To apply, students must provide: 1. A complete application form (available from the Folklore Program office); 2. A description of the student's research project and its relation to folklore; 3. A recommendation from the student's advisor.
column47: The Designated Emphasis in Folklore (DE) is a program for graduate students at UC Berkeley who are interested in the study of folklore and traditional culture. It is intended to provide a systematic and integrated curriculum of study for students who wish to pursue a concentration in folklore as part of their PhD program. The Designated Emphasis in Folklore is not a degree-granting program. Rather, it is an interdisciplinary program that offers a specialization in folklore to students who are already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Women, Gender, and Sexuality
column16: Only currently enrolled UC Berkeley PhD students are eligible to apply for a Designated Emphasis. Applicants must submit: 1. A complete Application for Admission to the Designated Emphasis in Women, Gender, and Sexuality. 2. A brief statement of purpose (no more than 2 pages) describing the student's research interests and its relationship to Women, Gender, and Sexuality. 3. A letter of recommendation from a member of the Women, Gender, and Sexuality Graduate Group who has agreed to serve on the student's exam and/or dissertation committee. 4. A curriculum vitae.
column38: Department of Gender and Women’s Studies
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Women, Gender, and Sexuality provides graduate students with the opportunity to specialize in women, gender, and sexuality studies while completing their PhD degree. It is designed to provide a formal structure for interdisciplinary work and to recognize the importance of research and teaching in this area. The DE offers students a program of study that includes a core course, electives, and a dissertation with a significant focus on women, gender, and/or sexuality.

column2: Designated Emphasis in European Studies
column16: To be eligible for the Designated Emphasis in European Studies, students must be enrolled in an existing PhD program at UC Berkeley. Admission is by application to the DE Committee. Required documents for the application include a completed application form, a statement of purpose (no more than 2 pages) describing the student’s interest in European Studies and how it relates to their doctoral research, a letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor in their home department, and a curriculum vitae.
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in European Studies is available to Berkeley Ph.D. students in any department or program. It provides an opportunity for students to engage in interdisciplinary research on Europe, and to have that expertise recognized with a formal credential. Students must satisfy requirements in three categories: course work, a required language, and a dissertation with a European focus. Students should apply as soon as they decide to pursue the DE. The latest a student can apply is one semester before the Ph.D. qualifying exam.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Nanoscale Science and Engineering
column16: Admission to the DE is by application to the DE Graduate Group. To be eligible to apply, students must be in good standing in a participating PhD program. Ideally, students should apply for the DE after their first or second year of graduate study, but before taking the PhD Qualifying Exam. Application requirements include: 1. Completion of the application form including the signature of the student’s PhD advisor. 2. Preparation of a 1-2 page statement of interest that includes: a description of the student’s research interests and its relationship to Nanoscale Science and Engineering, and how the student intends to fulfill the DE requirements (including a proposed list of courses). 3. Letter of Recommendation from the PhD advisor.
column38: Nanoscale Science and Engineering Graduate Group
column47: The Nanoscale Science and Engineering Graduate Group (NSEGG) offers a Designated Emphasis (DE) in Nanoscale Science and Engineering (NSE). The DE in NSE is an interdisciplinary program that provides graduate students with a comprehensive education in the fundamental science and engineering of nanoscale structures. NSE is a rapidly growing field with profound implications for technology, medicine, and the environment. The program aims to train the next generation of researchers and leaders in this exciting field, fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration and providing students with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in this competitive landscape.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Energy Sciences and Technology
column11: No later than the semester before the student’s qualifying exam
column16: To apply for the Designated Emphasis in Energy Science and Technology (DEEST), students must: 1. Be a doctoral student in good standing at UC Berkeley. 2. Be enrolled in a PhD program in one of the participating departments (College of Engineering, College of Chemistry, College of Natural Resources, or Department of Physics). 3. Complete the DEEST Application Form. 4. Provide a one-page statement of interest. 5. Provide a letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor. 6. Provide a transcript (unofficial is okay).
column47: The Designated Emphasis in Energy Science and Technology (DEEST) is an interdisciplinary program that provides a framework for doctoral students to specialize in energy science and technology. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of energy science and technology, and to introduce them to the social, economic, and policy aspects of energy systems. The DEEST provides an opportunity for doctoral students from a variety of engineering and science departments to engage in a curriculum that includes energy-related coursework and research.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics
column16: To be admitted to the DE in Communication, Computation, and Statistics (CCS), a student must already be enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. Students should apply to the DE as early as possible in their graduate career, but no later than the semester of their PhD Qualifying Examination. To apply, students must submit an application form, a letter of support from their PhD advisor, and a short statement of interest.
column47: The Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics (DECCS) provides students with a strong background in the methods of communication, computation, and statistics, as applied to the social sciences. The DECCS is intended for doctoral students in social science departments (e.g., Sociology, Political Science, Economics, etc.) who want to learn how to apply these methods to their research. The DECCS provides a curriculum that covers the fundamentals of communication, computation, and statistics, as well as more advanced topics in these areas. Students who complete the DECCS will be well-prepared for careers in academia, government, and the private sector. Upon successful completion of the dissertation and the DECCS requirements, the student’s transcript will include the notation ‘Designated Emphasis in Communication, Computation and Statistics’.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Computational and Genomic Biology
column16: To be admitted to the DE, students must already be enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. The student must have the support of his/her PhD advisor to join the DE, and the student’s PhD advisor must be a core or affiliate faculty member of the Center for Computational Biology. Application consists of an application form, a one-page statement of interest, and a letter of support from the student’s faculty advisor.
column47: Computational biology is a central field in modern biology. The Designated Emphasis in Computational and Genomic Biology (DE CGB) is intended to provide curriculum and training in the field to students in doctoral programs across the Berkeley campus. The DE CGB provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of biology, statistics, and computer science, as well as the ability to apply these principles to the analysis of genomic data.

column2: Designated Emphasis in New Media
column16: To be eligible for the Designated Emphasis in New Media, students must be enrolled in a Ph.D. program at UC Berkeley. Admission to the DE is by application to the Berkeley Center for New Media. Students are encouraged to apply for the DE as early as possible in their doctoral studies, and MUST apply prior to their qualifying examination.
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in New Media provides Berkeley doctoral students with a set of curricular and research resources for studying the impact of new media on traditional disciplines. It is an interdisciplinary program that involves more than two dozen faculty from across the campus. The DE provides students with a common set of theoretical and methodological tools for research on new media and brings them into a community of researchers who are exploring the field.
column101: Merit-based

column2: Designated Emphasis in Global Urban Humanities
column16: To be admitted to the DE, students must already be enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. Application requirements include a completed application form, a brief (1-2 page) letter of intent addressed to the GUH DE Admissions Committee describing the student’s research interest in the DE and their relevant background, an unofficial transcript of UC Berkeley coursework, and a letter of support from the student’s faculty advisor in their home department.
column47: The Graduate Designated Emphasis (DE) in Global Urban Humanities provides an interdisciplinary framework for the study of the city. Students investigate the histories and cultures of cities as they interact with the physical and social environments. The curriculum includes a core course, Global Urban Humanities: Theories and Methods, and two electives, as well as an interdisciplinary research studio. The DE allows students in the humanities, social sciences, and environmental design to engage in shared study and research, bridging the gap between descriptive and interpretive methods and the projective and diagnostic tools of the design and planning disciplines. Students in PhD programs across the campus are eligible to apply.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Development Engineering
column16: To be eligible, students must be currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. The application consists of a statement of interest (no more than 2 pages) describing the student’s research interests and how they relate to development engineering, a letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor, and a list of courses that will be used to satisfy the Designated Emphasis requirements.
column47: Development Engineering (DE) is an interdisciplinary field that addresses the problems of people living in poverty. Building on the core strengths of UC Berkeley in engineering and the social sciences, the program focuses on creating technology-based solutions to solve global development problems. The DE provides students with a set of tools to create, pilot, and evaluate technology that could improve the lives of those in low-resource settings. Students learn how to measure the impact of their work and how to think about the economic and social context of their technical solutions.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Science and Technology Studies
column16: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Science and Technology Studies is an interdisciplinary program of study open to students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley. Students are required to take a core course, three electives, and include an STS faculty member on their qualifying exam and dissertation committees. To apply for admission to the DE in STS, please submit: A 1–2 page Statement of Purpose describing your interest in STS and the relationship of the DE to your program of study. An application form. A letter of recommendation from a member of the STS affiliated faculty who is willing to serve as your DE advisor. A memo or email from your Head Graduate Advisor in your home department confirming that you are a student in good standing and that they have no objection to your participating in the DE.
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Science and Technology Studies (STS) provides a curated course of study for Berkeley PhD students who want to develop a rigorous, interdisciplinary approach to their work. The program is designed to provide students with a theoretical and methodological foundation in the social studies of science, technology and medicine. It is intended to help students from a wide range of disciplines to communicate with researchers from other fields, and to facilitate the development of a common set of questions and research methods. The DE will provide students with a formal credential in STS, and will help to create a community of scholars who are interested in the social and cultural dimensions of science and technology. Students who complete the DE will be better prepared to participate in the global conversation about the role of science and technology in society, and will be better positioned for academic and professional opportunities in this growing field.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies
column16: Graduate students already admitted to a PhD program at UC Berkeley are eligible to apply. Designated Emphases (DE) are specialized concentrations available to doctoral students in certain programs. Students must already be admitted to a Berkeley PhD program to apply for a DE. To apply, students must have the support of a faculty member who is affiliated with the Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies and who will serve on the student’s qualifying exam and dissertation committees. The application must be submitted before the qualifying examination.
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Dutch Studies is a program that provides a framework for regular and structured contact among graduate students and faculty in different disciplines who study Dutch history, culture, linguistics, and literature. The Dutch Studies program is unique in its breadth and its interdisciplinary nature. Its goals are: To provide a structure for graduate students who would like to study Dutch history, culture, linguistics, or literature in a more formal way. To foster an interdisciplinary approach to Dutch Studies and to create a community of scholars who work in these areas. For students who choose this DE, the PhD degree will be designated with the name of the home department and the program, for example: “PhD in History with a Designated Emphasis in Dutch Studies.”

column2: Designated Emphasis in Indigenous Language Revitalization
column16: To apply, students should submit to the Chair of the Graduate Group in Indigenous Language Revitalization (ilr@berkeley.edu): A statement of purpose (maximum two pages), A letter of recommendation from the student’s faculty advisor, and A letter of recommendation from another faculty member who is part of the Indigenous Language Revitalization Graduate Group. Students should apply for admission to the Indigenous Language Revitalization Graduate Group at any time after their first semester and no later than the semester before their qualifying exam.
column47: The Designated Emphasis in Indigenous Language Revitalization (DEILR) is an interdisciplinary program that offers graduate students from any department at UC Berkeley the opportunity to gain expertise in the theory and practice of language revitalization. The program is designed to prepare students for academic and professional work in this field by providing them with a solid foundation in the linguistic, pedagogical, and social aspects of language revitalization.

column2: Designated Emphasis in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies
column16: Admission to the DE is by application. Students should apply in their second or third year of study, but must be admitted to the DE before taking the qualifying examination. Requirements for admission: 1. Application form. 2. Statement of interest (no more than 2 pages) explaining the student’s interest in the DE and describing the student’s research and how it will involve interdisciplinary study in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies. 3. Letter of recommendation from the student’s PhD advisor. 4. Writing sample (e.g., a paper for a course, or a draft of a dissertation chapter). 5. Curriculum Vitae (CV).
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Renaissance and Early Modern Studies (REMS) provides a framework for regular exchange among faculty and graduate students in different departments at Berkeley and a way to coordinate and foster the interdisciplinary study of the early modern period (roughly 1350–1750). The Designated Emphasis is open to graduate students already enrolled in a Ph.D. program in any department or school at UC Berkeley. Since 2001, students from Architecture, Comparative Literature, English, French, German, History, History of Art, Italian Studies, Music, Near Eastern Studies, Philosophy, Rhetoric, South and Southeast Asian Studies, and Spanish and Portuguese have been part of the program.
column101: Travel Grants, Summer Research Grants

column2: Designated Emphasis in Southeast Asian Studies
column16: Only students already enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley are eligible for the Designated Emphasis. To be admitted to the DE, students must: 1. Be admitted to a PhD program at UC Berkeley. 2. Submit an application form signed by the student’s head graduate adviser in their home department. 3. Submit a statement of intent (approximately two pages) that explains how the student’s research interest and dissertation relate to Southeast Asian studies. 4. Have a member of the DE Graduate Group on their dissertation committee.
column47: The Designated Emphasis (DE) in Southeast Asian Studies (SEAS) provides a framework for regularized interdisciplinary collaboration and for the professional certification of graduate students who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at UC Berkeley and whose work has a significant focus on Southeast Asia. There is a growing number of doctoral students at Berkeley in various departments and disciplines who work on some aspect of Southeast Asia. Often these students have few opportunities to interact with each other, and they frequently feel somewhat isolated within their own departments. The Designated Emphasis in Southeast Asian Studies aims to create a community of Southeast Asianists on the Berkeley campus. Its main goal is to promote a multi-disciplinary approach to Southeast Asian studies by providing students with a systematic way of identifying a core of faculty and other students with whom they can work as they proceed through their training.
column101: Merit-based (Foreign Language and Area Studies Fellowships)

column2: Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science
column16: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science is open to any current UC Berkeley graduate student. To be eligible, students must be currently enrolled in a UC Berkeley graduate degree program (Master’s or Ph.D.) and be in good academic standing. Applicants are required to submit a brief statement of interest and complete an online application.
column47: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Data Science is a program for UC Berkeley graduate students in any department. The certificate program allows students to gain the skills they need to navigate the world of data and big data. Students learn the latest techniques for collecting, cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing data, and gain experience with a wide range of data science tools and technologies.

column2: Graduate Certificate in Food Systems
column8: Rolling (Any time during the academic year)
column16: Only currently enrolled UC Berkeley graduate students in good standing are eligible to apply. To apply, please complete the Graduate Certificate in Food Systems Intent to Apply form. Certificate requirements include: one 3-unit core course (either PB HLTH 204 or ESPM 230), elective courses totaling at least 8 units from at least two of three categories (Social & Economic, Environmental, and Public Health), and one capstone/integrated project.
column38: College of Natural Resources, School of Public Health, and College of Environmental Design
column47: The Graduate Certificate in Food Systems is an interdisciplinary program that allows graduate students to gain a broad and comprehensive understanding of the complex factors that influence food systems. This certificate program is open to all graduate students at UC Berkeley and is designed to provide students with the necessary tools to address the multifaceted challenges of creating a more sustainable, equitable, and healthy food system. The certificate provides a framework for students to explore how different aspects of food systems—from production and processing to distribution and consumption—are interconnected and influence health, environment, and society. Students will develop the skills to analyze and address these complexities through interdisciplinary coursework and a capstone project.

column2: Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities
column16: The Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities is open to all UC Berkeley graduate students in good standing in any department. To apply, students must submit an Application Form, a Statement of Interest (max 500 words) describing research interests and how they relate to the certificate, and a short bio (max 100 words).
column47: The Graduate Certificate in Global Urban Humanities is a certificate program for UC Berkeley graduate students in any department who are interested in the study of cities and urban life through a combination of humanistic and design/social science methods. The program is part of the Global Urban Humanities Initiative, a joint project of the Arts & Humanities Division and the College of Environmental Design. The certificate provides a framework for students to engage in interdisciplinary research and pedagogy, offering a curriculum that includes an introductory core colloquium, elective courses from departments outside the student's home discipline, and a research-intensive capstone requirement such as an interdisciplinary studio or research seminar.

column2: Graduate Certificate in Real Estate
column8: Rolling basis (Any time during graduate studies)
column11: Final semester of the student's degree program
column16: The Interdisciplinary Graduate Certificate in Real Estate (IGCRE) is available to any student currently enrolled in a graduate program at the University of California, Berkeley. To apply, students should submit the Intent to Register form as soon as they decide to pursue the IGCRE. To receive the certificate, students must successfully complete three courses: one from the 'Core' category (ARCH 268, LD ARCH 268, CY PLAN 213, or MBA 280) and two additional courses from the approved list, one of which must be outside the student's home department. All courses must be taken for a letter grade and a grade of B or better must be achieved. In the final semester of study, students must submit the Completion Form and a current transcript.
column38: Haas School of Business, College of Environmental Design, Berkeley Law School, and Goldman School of Public Policy
column40: $0 (The Graduate Certificate in Real Estate is an add-on to the degree program and does not have any additional tuition or fees)
column47: The Graduate Certificate in Real Estate (GCRE) is available to any student currently enrolled in a graduate degree program at UC Berkeley. The certificate is a way to gain further knowledge in real estate that may not be available in their home department, and to give students a competitive edge in the job market. It is an interdisciplinary program that includes the Haas School of Business, the College of Environmental Design, the Berkeley Law School, and the Goldman School of Public Policy. The certificate is administered by the Fisher Center for Real Estate and Urban Economics at the Haas School of Business.
column57: 3.0 (Grade of B or better in all course requirements)

column2: Graduate Certificate in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education
column16: The Certificate Program in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education is open to currently enrolled UC Berkeley doctoral students. To receive the Certificate, students must: 1. Successfully complete the 300-level pedagogy course in their department. 2. Teach as a GSI for at least two semesters at UC Berkeley. 3. Participate in at least six qualifying workshops sponsored by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center or other Graduate Division programs. 4. Be observed teaching by a faculty member who provides a written report to the student. 5. Develop a teaching portfolio that meets the criteria established by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center.
column38: GSI Teaching & Resource Center, Graduate Division
column47: The Certificate in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education provides a structure for GSIs to refine their teaching skills and to provide them with a credential for the academic job market. The program is sponsored by the GSI Teaching & Resource Center and the Graduate Council of the Academic Senate. To receive the certificate, participants must complete a sequence of activities: a pedagogy course, teaching experience, teaching observations, and a teaching portfolio. The certificate program aims to: (1) assist GSIs in enhancing their teaching while at UC Berkeley, (2) prepare GSIs for the teaching responsibilities they will assume as future faculty, (3) provide GSIs with a credential for the job market, and (4) identify GSIs on campus who have a significant commitment to teaching and learning.
